name: Cult of the Damned
summary: The Cult of the Damned is a secretive cabal of mortal zealots, necromancers, and aristocrats devoted to the Lich King. Formed in northern Lordaeron prior to the Third War, its members poisoned the grain supplies that spawned the Scourge and engineered the downfall of humanity's greatest kingdom. Today, the surviving cultists manage the plague cauldrons and necromantic academies across the Plaguelands while actively infiltrating the cities of the living.

sections.title: A Sickness in the Soul
sections.body: The Cult of the Damned was forged by the exiled Archmage Kel'Thuzad after he answered the telepathic whispers of the Lich King emanating from the Frozen Throne. Returning to Lordaeron with vast wealth and forbidden dark arts, Kel'Thuzad offered two false gospels: to the desperate, impoverished lower classes, he promised social equality and liberation from misery; to the wealthy landowners, such as the noble House of Barov, he promised eternal life and an unshakeable grip upon their domains. In truth, both the destitute and the affluent were cattle intended for slaughter, bound into a death cult designed to betray their homeland from the inside.

sections.title: The Poisoned Harvest
sections.body: Operating in complete secrecy from the dungeons beneath Caer Darrow, the cultists honed their necrotic craft, built hulking abominations, and perfected the Plague of Undeath brought south from Northrend. They struck at Lordaeron's breadbasket, contaminating the grain stores at Andorhal. As tainted flour traveled through regular merchant routes to hearths across the Eastweald, commoners sickened and died within days, only to rise as shambling thralls under the Lich King's telepathic lash. When Prince Arthas slaughtered Kel'Thuzad in Andorhal, the cultist network was already so deeply rooted that the kingdom's doom was sealed.

sections.title: The Present Threat
sections.body: Though Arthas sailed to Northrend and ascended the Frozen Throne, the Cult of the Damned remains fully operational in northern Lordaeron under the command of the resurrected archlich Kel'Thuzad. From the shadows of Stratholme and the halls of Scholomance, living cultists perform dark rites, maintain the toxic plague cauldrons across the ruined farmsteads, and attempt to assassinate Scarlet Crusaders and Forsaken alike. Because they still breathe, these acolytes can walk unnoticed through living settlements, poisoning wells, sabotaging supply lines, and grooming new recruits to feed the Scourge machine.

faq.q: Why would living mortals join a cult that turns people undead?
aliases: why join cult of the damned
faq.answer: Kel'Thuzad preyed upon mortal weakness. He offered the impoverished lower classes a new order of absolute equality and relief from their hardships, while promising wealthy nobles like Baron Rivendare and the Barov family immortality and everlasting power. Most initiates were kept ignorant of the true, horrific nature of the plague until it was too late to turn back.

faq.q: Why are cultists allowed to stay alive instead of being killed and raised?
faq.answer: Living agents possess immense practical value for the Lich King. They can pass through human settlements unnoticed, trade along standard merchant lines, purchase supplies, and subvert kingdoms from within. In cult doctrine, undeath is also treated as a glorious reward that must be earned through devoted service.

faq.q: Where is the Cult of the Damned based?
faq.answer: Their primary scholastic and spiritual redoubt is Scholomance, located within the catacombs beneath Caer Darrow. Beyond this academy, large concentrations of cultists operate in the ruins of Stratholme, around the plague cauldrons of the Western and Eastern Plaguelands, and across secret cells hidden in living settlements.

faq.q: Who founded the Cult of the Damned?
faq.answer: Archmage Kel'Thuzad, a former high-ranking member of Dalaran's Kirin Tor. After being censured for his forbidden necromantic studies, he traveled north to commune with the Lich King, who granted him immense power and sent him back to Lordaeron to organize the mortal vanguard of the Scourge.

faq.q: How does the Cult of the Damned spread the plague today?
faq.answer: While they initially spread the plague through tainted grain shipments from Andorhal, they now primarily rely on massive plague cauldrons situated across Plaguelands farms. Cultist cauldron lords brew foul reagents to continuously release noxious clouds of blight that choke the land and raise fallen corpses.

faq.q: What is the cult's relationship to the Forsaken?
faq.answer: They are bitter enemies. The Forsaken broke free from the Lich King's telepathic command and seek vengeance against the Scourge. Cultists view the Forsaken as stolen property and heretics, constantly seeking to annihilate them or reclaim the ruins of Lordaeron for the Frozen Throne.

angles.text: Every human remembers the collapse of Lordaeron; the Cult of the Damned serves as a bitter reminder that humanity was not conquered by demons alone, but by traitors from within their own cities and estates.
To the Forsaken, cultists are pathetic lapdogs who willingly sacrifice their freedom to the master whose mental chains the Forsaken fought so hard to shatter.
The Cult of the Damned represents the ultimate blasphemy against the Holy Light, wielding foul necromancy to corrupt the living and disturb the eternal rest of the dead.
The cult is a painful stain on the honor of the Kirin Tor, having been founded by one of Dalaran's own esteemed archmages, Kel'Thuzad.
Alliance scouts and soldiers must remain constantly vigilant, as cult infiltrators still attempt to sow plague and chaos inside living cities like Stormwind.
